output:
To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT – Handover for Inês: Thursday 26 November launch

Inês,

My father is ill, I am with my family. I am taking the train tonight and I do not know how long I will be away. You can call me, but after 09:00 tomorrow, Tuesday 24 November, I might not pick up. If you cannot reach me, please do not wait for my approval: make the decision and tell me later.

Before the practical list: I am very sorry to leave you with both the launch and a late correction. The EUR 2.1 billion mistake is mine, not yours. I found it only this afternoon. If anyone asks whose error it was, please say that plainly.

I also want you to hear this directly from me, rather than infer it from a handover note: I trust you completely. You know the paper as well as I do, and you ran the annex B sensitivity analysis yourself. You are not simply reading out my presentation on Thursday; you are the right person to present and defend the work. I still think about the COP side event in Lisbon, when the projector died and you rescued my panel. You are better live than you think. Use your own wording, cut anything that does not fit, and own the room.

Your priorities, in order, are:

1. Stop the incorrect 2.1 figure from reaching anyone else, and correct everything already in circulation before the embargo lifts.
2. Confirm the changed running order, speaker arrangements and badges with Tomás.
3. Prepare a presentation that comfortably fits 15 minutes, then present and join the panel.
4. Make sure Hanna has a workable arrangements for the press calls, photographs and attendance follow-up.

1. The figure 3 correction comes first

The corrected 2030 LDC-relevant revenue figure is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion.

The old number came from the previous run, in which the free-allocation phase-out was not applied. Figure 3 and the summary were affected. The conclusion of the paper does not change, but the headline number does.

PDF v7 in the launch folder is corrected on pages 3, 14 and 15. Treat that as the source of truth. There is no need to reopen the model or rerun the analysis.

Still outstanding:

- Deck v4: slides 6 and 9 still contain the error. Slide 9 is the revenue chart. Check the speaker notes and search the whole deck for “2.1” and other repetitions of the old headline, rather than only replacing the chart. Save a clearly marked corrected version so nobody presents v4 by accident.
- Press release: the embargoed version Hanna sent to our 34 Brussels contacts on Friday still says 2.1. The embargo lifts on Thursday 26 November at 10:00 CET. Please speak to Hanna first thing Tuesday and ask her to send a clearly marked correction to the same list as soon as possible, with the embargo time unchanged. Journalists should be asked to discard the earlier version and use only the corrected release. Do not leave this until Wednesday or Thursday morning.
- Sign-off: Geert knows I am away. If Hanna needs a senior name to approve the corrected press release, go directly to Geert Lammens. You do not need to wait for me.
- Final check: before Wednesday evening, confirm with Hanna that the corrected PDF, corrected deck and corrected release are the versions being used, and that nothing containing 2.1 is still scheduled to go out.

If a journalist asks about the change, the answer is factual and short: the earlier figure came from an old run; the corrected report gives EUR 1.4 billion; the conclusion is unchanged. There is no reason to hide the correction or to turn it into a bigger story than it is.

2. Tuesday: confirm the event and communications arrangements

Write to Tomás Reyes (tomas.reyes@ep-office-lindqvist.example), copying Hanna if useful, and cover all of the following in one exchange:

- Tell him that I will not be there and that you will give the presentation and take my place on the panel.
- Accept the shorter presentation: 15 minutes rather than 20.
- Confirm the panel start at 12:50.
- Lindqvist now has to leave at 13:30 because of a moved vote and wants to take at least two audience questions herself before she goes. Ask Tomás to agree exactly where those questions will fit and who will moderate or close the event after she leaves.
- Ask him to confirm that the 14:00 close still stands.
- Send the final names of everyone attending from our side well before his hard deadline of Wednesday 25 November at 12:00. Security will not admit anyone whose name is missing. Ideally settle this on Tuesday with Hanna rather than using the full deadline.

Separately, agree with Hanna who will handle badges, photographs, attendance numbers and any last-minute journalist queries. Please do not end up doing all of that yourself while also preparing to speak.

3. Wednesday: finish the content, then stop tinkering

There are two background press calls in my calendar for Wednesday at 14:00 and 15:00, by phone, 20 minutes each. One journalist is from a trade newsletter and one from a Belgian daily. Hanna had told them I would be available.

Ask her either to move the calls to you or to rearrange them. If you take them, lead with the corrected EUR 1.4 billion figure and make sure they have received the corrected release. If doing both calls would compromise your preparation, Hanna should move them; they are not more important than a clean launch.

For the presentation:

- Reduce deck v4 further rather than trying to deliver all 14 slides at speed. Fifteen minutes is now the limit.
- Keep your speaker notes in your own words. My notes are in the deck, but they are a starting point, not a script.
- Rehearse once with the questions and answers you are most likely to use, and once against the clock.
- Check that only the corrected deck is on the laptop or other system being used in the room.
- Abena’s remote link is in the calendar invite. She tested it and it worked, but allow time for a final sound and connection check before guests settle.

Once the corrected release is out, the deck works and the badges are settled, let the small things go.

4. Thursday: running order

All times below are CET.

- Before 10:00: confirm with Hanna that the corrected release is with all 34 original recipients.
- 10:00: embargo lifts.
- Arrive early enough to check the corrected deck, microphone and Abena’s remote connection.
- 12:00: guests must be at the Parliament security entrance. Tomás is collecting badges. A light lunch is available outside the room.
- 12:30: Katarina Lindqvist welcomes everyone, five minutes.
- 12:35: your presentation, 15 minutes.
- 12:50: panel with you, Dr Abena Owusu-Mensah remotely, and Florian Kessler of the Alliance of European Steel Users. Lindqvist moderates.
- Before 13:30: make sure the agreed arrangement gives Lindqvist at least two audience questions.
- 13:30: Lindqvist leaves. Continue under whatever chairing arrangement Tomás confirms.
- 14:00: close, unless Tomás has agreed a different arrangement.

The venue is the Altiero Spinelli building, in the room booked by Lindqvist’s office. The paper being launched is “Who Pays at the Border? CBAM revenues and the least developed countries”.

5. Kessler and the likely difficult questions

Kessler will try to make the discussion about the 80% pass-through assumption. Do not let him set the tone for the whole launch or make one modelling assumption sound like the entire paper.

The answer is already in the work:

- The 80% figure is the central case in section 4, not a claim that every company can pass through exactly 80%.
- Annex B tests 40% and 60%. You ran those sensitivities yourself.
- The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. Say that openly. Do not get defensive and do not improvise a new estimate.
- Acknowledge the position of smaller manufacturers, answer the substance once, and then bring the discussion back to the paper’s treatment of LDCs and its conclusions.
- On resource shuffling, we agree that it is a risk. Section 5.2 addresses it, and we recommend the Commission’s monitoring report. There is no need to dispute that risk simply because Kessler raises it.

Abena is likely to be strong on the LDC side. Give her room to make her own argument rather than treating her as support we have scripted.

If the figure correction comes up in the room, stay calm: the current report and presentation use EUR 1.4 billion, the earlier 2.1 figure came from an old run, and the conclusion is unchanged. If anyone asks responsibility, the mistake was mine, not yours.

6. After the event

Lucy Tran from the Halvorsen Foundation will attend with a colleague. For their grant report, she needs two photographs from the event and the attendance numbers, ideally by Friday 4 December. Her address is lucy.tran@halvorsen-foundation.example. Ask Hanna or someone else attending to capture these during the event so you can concentrate on the discussion, then make sure they are sent to Lucy.

Everything else can wait until we have had a proper debrief.

I am sorry again that you are inheriting this at such short notice. But there is no one I would rather have presenting the paper or handling the questions. You do not need to protect me, reproduce my delivery, or ask permission for every judgment. You know the work, you know where its limits are, and you have already proved that you can handle a room when the plan falls apart.

Thank you, Inês. I am sorry, and I trust you completely.

Marieke
